title: The starter is the bakery
thesis: The slow invisible part of the work decides the result, long before anyone sees it.

nodes.text: To team leads: a note about what gets praised, and what never gets seen.
What prompts the letter now? The brief names the reader but no occasion (a review cycle, a launch, a specific team moment).
The month of feeding the starter is the work nobody watches, and it is where the loaf is decided: a weak starter cannot be rescued at the oven.

evidence.filled_by: transcript s1 line 5: "If the starter is weak, the loaves come out flat and sour and nobody can fix that at the oven."

nodes.text: The eleven years of notebooks are the same kind of work at a longer scale: slow, unseen, and the reason the result is good.
Whose notebooks are they, and what is in them? The brief requires them but the material I have doesn't say.
The person who knows the craft can tell who will be good from how they treat the slow part, not from the finished loaf.

evidence.filled_by: transcript s2 line 9: "That was the moment she knew he would be good."

nodes.text: Who are "she" and "he", and what did he do in that moment? The quote is the turn but the brief doesn't carry the scene.
The ask: before you praise the loaf, find out who fed the starter, and protect that work on your team.

evidence.filled_by: brief purpose (writer, rev 3): "Make readers protect the unglamorous early work on their teams."

nodes.text: Should the ask name a workplace equivalent of the starter, or leave the translation to the reader? The brief gives no team example.
